blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Nearly half of the Philippine population could not afford a healthy diet in 2025, with an estimated 52.6 million people unable to pay for enough nutritious food after covering other essential household expenses, according to data from the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO). In an analysis of the figures, Inquirer data scientist and University of the Philippines (UP) Diliman associate professor Dr. Rogelio Alicor Panao said the estimate placed the Philippines among the countries with the largest populations struggling to afford a nutritious diet.
